findings.criterion: Every edge in the table is exercised by the same test for both `claim` and `transition`; checked by a parametrised test over the table.
findings.detail: No `@pytest.mark.parametrize` decorator was found in either `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_claim_transition_parent_cascade.py` or `tests/unit/commands/test_lifecycle_cascade.py`. The criterion explicitly requires 'a parametrised test over the table' that exercises every edge for both claim and transition surfaces. The test suite contains individual named tests for each edge and surface (e.g., test_claim_child_claims_open_parent_first, test_transition_child_to_in_progress_cascades_to_open_parent, test_reopen_child_reopens_closed_parent, test_reactivate_child_reactivates_closed_parent), but no single parametrized test that iterates over the _CASCADING_EDGES table entries and exercises both claim and transition for each.
findings.remediation: Add a @pytest.mark.parametrize test that iterates over _CASCADING_EDGES entries and exercises both claim and transition for each edge.
findings.title: No parametrised test over the _CASCADING_EDGES table for both claim and transition

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[non-codebase]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
